customManagers.description: SCANNER_IMAGE is a plain `docker run` argument in ci.yml/release.yml, not a `uses:` reference, so the github-actions manager does not see it. It must keep moving with the SecObserve action pins it sits next to - see docs/adr/0007-secobserve-upload-correctness.md.

packageRules.description: Go modules settle before they are proposed, and every update tidies the module it touched.

e2e is a separate module with a `replace` to ../, so every direct dependency of the root module is an indirect one of e2e's. Renovate does not manage indirect Go dependencies by default, so without this e2e/go.mod silently keeps the old versions every time the root module is bumped and `go vet ./...` in e2e/ fails with "updates to go.mod needed" - see PR #50. Enabling them lets Renovate bump and tidy e2e in the same PR as the root change.
The AWS SDK ships ~20 modules that share internal versions; a partial bump does not compile, so they move together or not at all.
otel, its metric/sdk packages and the exporters are one release train.
Container-backed test harness only. These cannot reach the production binary and drag ~89 transitive modules of their own, so they are grouped away from everything that can.

The Go toolchain changes codegen and runtime behaviour for everything it builds. It is never a routine bump and must not ride along with a library update - PR #50 bundled go 1.25 -> 1.26 with the whole AWS SDK.
Base images are pinned by digest; a rebuild changes what ships, but CI now has to pass first.
Actions are pinned to a commit sha. Since the CI rework these push images to GHCR and sign with this repository's OIDC identity, so automerge waits on CI (see the removal of ignoreTests).
A major action bump can rename inputs, so it waits for a person.
